explanation: The map is drawn as if seen from above the North Pole and stops at 60 degrees south, so Antarctica is left off. The General Assembly adopted the flag in 1947.

claims.text: The flag of the United Nations shows a white map of the world framed by olive branches, on a light blue field.
The flag of the European Union shows a circle of gold stars on blue, with no world map and no olive branches.
The flag of the African Union shows a map of Africa, not of the world, and no olive branches.
The flag of the Red Cross is a red cross on white, with no map and no olive branches.
The map on the UN emblem is an azimuthal equidistant projection centred on the North Pole, as if seen from above the pole.
The map on the UN emblem extends only to 60 degrees south latitude, so Antarctica is not shown.
The UN General Assembly adopted the UN flag in 1947, by resolution 167 (II) of 20 October 1947.
